This is a real subagent delegation test inside the current disposable workspace. Use your native task tool to launch exactly TWO separate general-purpose subagent invocations, preferably concurrently. Do not perform their file operations yourself and do not simulate delegation using shell processes.
Delegate A: Work only in /opt/agent/workspace/subagent-test/alpha. Create its directory and draft.txt, write exactly ALPHA_CREATED on line 1, append ALPHA_WRITTEN on line 2, create an archive directory, then MOVE draft.txt to archive/final.txt. Verify original is absent and report final contents and tools used.
Delegate B: Independently work only in /opt/agent/workspace/subagent-test/beta. Create its directory and draft.txt, write exactly BETA_CREATED on line 1, append BETA_WRITTEN on line 2, create an archive directory, then MOVE draft.txt to archive/final.txt. Verify original is absent and report final contents and tools used.
Both subagents must execute actual filesystem/shell tools, not just provide instructions. Do not access network services, credentials, or files outside these task directories. After both finish, you may independently read the two final files and verify the original paths are absent. Report both delegation outcomes. If task is unavailable or fails, report that honestly; do not replace delegation with doing everything yourself.
